notes: Access: direct fetch worked throughout (no WAF/challenge, robots.txt has generic Disallow: / with explicit Allow for /, /products/, /collections/ etc - no Claude-specific block). Site is a headless Next.js storefront over a Shopify backend (cdn.shopify.com assets) - standard /collections/<handle>/products.json is NOT exposed (404), so Rule 1's usual 'enumerate via products.json' route is unavailable. Verification method used instead: each collection page renders a genuine 'N Products' summary AND real server-rendered pagination (?page=2..M); page size is a fixed 20/page confirmed from the embedded grid JSON (product 'handle' fields in the RSC payload, e.g. clocks page 1 = exactly 20 distinct handles). For every extracted category I performed an exhaustion check: ceil(displayed_count/20) was compared to the actual last pagination link on the page, and all 19 matched exactly (e.g. Lamps & Lighting 10311 Products -> last link page=516 = ceil(10311/20); Serveware 8285 -> page=415; Wall Decor 20224 -> page=1012; Clocks 2052 -> page=103; etc). This is a real per-collection exhaustion check, not a trust of a raw inflatable field - counts treated as verified. Large counts are explained (and cross-checked) by the sitemap: sitemap.xml lists 36 sitemap_products_N.xml files (35 x 2500 + 1 x 885 = ~88,385 total product URLs sitewide), and product-detail sampling confirmed the site models each colour/variant as a SEPARATE product page (e.g. Ashtrays: barca-ash-tray, barca-ash-tray-blue, barca-ash-tray-green, barca-ash-tray-purple = 4 distinct product URLs for one design) - this is why single categories like Lamps & Lighting (10311) or Wall Decor (20224) run into five figures; it is a real count of real distinct listed product pages, not a products_count API artifact. Rule 0: no room-based lighting hierarchy exists on this site (Lamps & Lighting is a single flat collection with only material/style/colour facets, no room sub-nav found in the embedded filter data) - emitted as one leaf row. Exclusions applied: Candles & Aroma (candles-aroma, 780) - sample titles dominated by scented/soy-wax/gift-box candles (Home Fragrance exclusion), kept separate from the in-scope Candle Stand & Holders collection. Bottles & Tumblers (bottles-tumblers, 1275) - reusable hydration bottles/tumblers (steel/plastic), not decorative glassware - excluded as kitchenware/hydration, not tableware. Barware (barware, 1252) - mixed roll-up of bar tools (bartender sets, bar spoons), beer mugs and ashtrays; the true glassware items within it are already covered by the standalone Glassware collection, so the whole roll-up was dropped per 'mixed roll-ups: drop, don't pad'. Ashtrays (ashtrays, 127) - excluded as a smoking accessory, not in the decorative-accessories include list (bowls/trays/vases/etc.) and not tableware. Bathroom Accessories (283) and Soap Dish & Dispensers - excluded as bathroom fixtures/storage (ceramic soap-dispenser+dish sets, bath mirrors bundled as fixture sets). Racks & Shelves (587) - excluded as storage/organiser furniture (multipurpose organizers, microwave stands, countertop risers), not decorative wall shelving. Table Accessories/kitchen-linens, Cookware & Bakeware, Kitchen Tools, Cutlery, all Bedding/Bedsheets/Bath Linens/Bath Towels/Bath Mats/Curtains/Cushions/Rugs & Carpets/Diwan Sets/Sofa Covers, Accent Furnitures, Artificial Flowers/Plants, Storage & Organisers, Gardening Accessories, Plants & Seeds, all Gifts-by-* collections, and Kids Room Decor (mixed furniture/textile/toy roll-up, no standalone decor facet) - all excluded per standard scope/NEVER-EXTRACT rules. Two pairs of genuinely distinct, separately-clickable nav categories with overlapping underlying tags were both kept as their own rows (consistent with how this project treats real site nav nodes elsewhere, e.g. FOS Lighting c268): Wall Decor (20224) vs Wall Paintings (15207), and Showpieces & Vases (4989) vs Showpieces (2933); also Mugs, Cups & Drinkware (4426) vs Mugs & Cups (2529) vs Coffee Mugs (757) - the first of these three includes a minor presence of water bottles mixed into the 'Drinkware' tag but is overwhelmingly mugs/cups/cup-saucer sets so was kept. Religious & Spiritual Items (1930) kept in scope: sample titles are brass/bronze idols, marble Buddha showpieces, metal/resin urlis (decorative bowls) and decorative diyas - functionally decorative figurines/sculptures/bowls, not functional puja hardware. No duplicate-company signal - Vaaree is a distinct Indian home-decor/lifestyle DTC brand (vaaree.com), not previously seen in this batch.
